title: Wave 4 — Plugin surface: secret-setting masking, tool-renderer gap pin, working-message sanitization, key-hint strip
wave: Sóng 4 — Bề mặt plugin, chờ M2
one_line: Four small plugin-surface fixes: stop a secret plugin setting from painting itself in the enum row, pin the tool-renderer-override gap with a real fixture plugin, sanitize the plugin-supplied working message, and let a plugin contribute a key-hint strip. Three of the four are unblocked today; only the secret-persistence half waits on M2 WI-8a.
user_visible_effect: A plugin setting marked `secret: true` no longer shows its value when it is an enum, and no longer repaints the plaintext after you pick a new value. A plugin's working message can no longer punch a tab-shaped hole in the TUI. A plugin can add a keyboard hint to the status row. Separately, a test now proves a plugin CAN override the built-in grep tool renderer today, so a future refactor cannot quietly close that seam without turning CI red.
one_line_why_this_is_the_whole_job: Wave 4 is four independent seams, not one feature. A4 is split by its own dependency: the display half touches only the TUI overlay and is unblocked; the persistence half rewrites `setPluginSetting` and is blocked on M2 WI-8a, which is rewriting the exact same three methods onto a new Settings substrate. B1, B2 and B3 add no public API — B1 only *pins* an existing gap with a fixture so a refactor cannot silently close it, and B2/B3 are UI-context methods that already exist on `ExtensionUIContext` and are already wired end to end.

test_contract:
Four contracts, one per item, each with a named failure mode.

A4-DISPLAY — 'a plugin setting marked secret never shows its value'. Consumer: a user reading the settings panel. Regression it defends: the mask survives a round-trip. The test builds the settings items for a plugin whose manifest declares an enum setting with `secret: true` and a known value, asserts the painted row contains the mask and not the value, then drives the submenu select callback and asserts the row STILL contains the mask. The second half is the point: a build-time-only mask is red here, because settings-list.ts:797 reassigns `currentValue` on select. Also assert a non-secret enum still shows its value — that is the negative contract proving the mask is conditional, not a blanket '•'. Finally assert the existing protections by driving the string form path with an empty submit and checking the stored secret is byte-unchanged (this passes today; keep it as a regression pin on the `empty: "cancel"` + `initialValue: undefined` pair, which is what stops a blank save from erasing a secret).

B1 — 'a plugin can override a built-in tool renderer, and the seam stays open'. Consumer: any plugin author, plus the loader's module-identity guarantee. The test loads the fixture directory by path through `loadExtensions` and asserts `toolRenderers.grep` is the fixture's, not the built-in `grepToolRenderer` (tui/src/tools/grep.ts:241). Then three pinned invariants: (a) `@oh-my-pi/pi-tui/tools` still resolves through the export map, checked by the RESOLVER's behavior and not by reading package.json; (b) the `toolRenderers` record is still extensible at runtime — assign then restore in `afterEach` so this file cannot poison another; (c) the loader remap still hands the plugin-side import the SAME module object the host holds, asserted with `===` on the module object each side receives. The whole mechanism is module identity, so this must run under a real plugin load, not an in-process import — a static import of the fixture would make (c) a tautology.

B2 — 'a plugin working message cannot break TUI layout'. Consumer: every user with a plugin installed. Assert a message containing a real tab and 500 characters renders with no 0x09 byte anywhere in the output and a display width inside the row budget. Assert `undefined` restores the default. Assert setting the same string twice requests one render — this is the anti-cache-thrash gate, and it currently holds only because of a guard inside loader.ts.

B3 — 'a plugin can contribute a key hint, and only in interactive TUI'. Consumer: a user in vim normal mode. Assert the status row names the non-default key and its action; assert the width ladder is respected; assert the strip is ABSENT in RPC, ACP and headless. Absence assertions are load-bearing here, not decorative.

gate_can_fail: Yes. Three of the four gates are genuinely red before the work and green after. (A4) the round-trip assertion is red on a clean tree because settings-list.ts:797 reassigns `currentValue` on select, repainting the plaintext — a build-time-only mask does not turn it green. (B2) the tab-byte assertion is red because setWorkingMessage (:6645-6660) passes the plugin string to `loadingAnimation.setMessage` with zero sanitization. (B3) the hint-strip assertions are red because no such entry point exists. (B1) is the weakest gate and must be treated as such: it pins an already-working mechanism, so it is green before AND after on a clean tree. Its value is purely as a tripwire against a future refactor closing the seam — it cannot fail because of anything done in this wave, and it should not be counted as evidence that B1 accomplished work. The 'static echo' risk is real here and is why the fixture must be loaded by path: a static import would make the module-identity assertion vacuously true.

risk: The single most likely way to get this wrong is treating A4 as a one-line display fix. `secret?: boolean` already exists in BOTH the TUI schema (plugin-settings.ts:31) and the plugin manifest (plugins/types.ts:63), so there is nothing to add, and the obvious one-line change — mask the enum's `currentValue` at :167 — produces a passing first-render test and a shipped leak, because settings-list.ts:797 reassigns `currentValue` the moment the user picks a value, and the same reassignment also breaks the submenu preselection (createConfigEnumPanel feeds `currentValue` straight into SelectFormField). The mask only holds if it is structural, i.e. a separate painted field that the update path never touches. Second-place risk: on B1, an engineer sets `PI_BUNDLED=1` to exercise the remap at legacy-pi-compat.ts:2742 as the plan's dossier anchor suggests. That constant is read once at import, and under `bun test` the virtual-namespace branch is dead anyway — forcing it breaks from the first line.
open_questions: A4-DISPLAY test location. All four units under test live in packages/tui (settings-list.ts, plugin-settings.ts), but the plan names packages/coding-agent/test/plugin-settings-secret.test.ts. The seam is real — buildPluginConfigItems takes a PluginSettingsManager, and a coding-agent test can construct one against a temp dir — so this is a house-style call, not a correctness one. Follow the plan unless packages/tui/test already has a settings-list harness; whichever is chosen, the test must not import the fixture by a path the runtime does not use.

A4-PERSIST destination, and the plan gets this wrong in a way that costs real time. The plan states the repo has no secret store to fall back to, and infers from a grep for `keytar|keychain|safeStorage|encrypt` that none exists. It does: `~/.omp/agent/secrets.yml` and `<cwd>/.omp/secrets.yml`, loaded at `packages/coding-agent/src/secrets/index.ts:163-168`, backed by SecretObfuscator and a per-install key at `~/.omp/agent/secret-placeholder.key` (secrets/index.ts:16-53), documented at `docs/secrets.md:35-42`. The grep missed it because the store is a YAML file, not a keyring API. So the choice is NOT 'invent somewhere to put it' — it is: route secret plugin settings into secrets.yml, or give the Settings registry a secret-marked tier. A human must pick. The tradeoff is real: settings are typed and validated by the registry, secrets.yml is a separate untyped format, and routing through it means plugin settings stop being validated like everything else. Do not let A4-PERSIST start until this is answered.

Does A4-PERSIST even want a separate persistence tier, or is encrypt-at-rest the honest answer? secrets.yml is plaintext on disk with reversible placeholders for the MODEL path; it is a redaction system, not a vault. If a plugin secret is an API token, secrets.yml is still plaintext to anything that can read the file. This is a scope question for whoever owns the item, and it is out of scope for this wave.

B3's tmux-stub assertion (the one that proves A8 ordering) is dropped if A8 has not landed. Confirm with the A8 owner whether to defer the whole item or just that assertion; the plan treats the ordering proof as load-bearing, which argues for deferring.
